evidence: Decode row verdict cell: "bandwidth-bound (25 ms TPOT is a budget; ~21% achieved HBM util at the canonical point — 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9%)"; same row's Resource-tell cell: "high HBM util, low FLOP util"; table footnote: "not verdicts on the canonical 8×H100 host's bandwidth adequacy — under tensor parallelism the 140 GB is sharded, so each GPU only needs ~0.70 TB/s against its own ~3.35 TB/s."
issue: The row is internally contradictory: it issues the verdict 'bandwidth-bound' and prescribes the telemetry tell 'high HBM util' while its own derivation states the canonical operating point achieves only ~21% of peak HBM bandwidth. A kernel at 21% of peak bandwidth cannot simultaneously exhibit the row's 'high HBM util' tell, and the footnote concedes the 5.6-vs-3.35 comparison is 'not verdicts on the canonical host's bandwidth adequacy'. The verdict as printed would send a reader to buy bandwidth the canonical host does not need.
fix_instruction: Restate the verdict cell as a regime classification only ('memory-bound by intensity ~1 FLOP/byte << ridge ~295; weight-read bandwidth not binding at the canonical point'), move the 20.9%-utilization figure into the verdict cell, and relabel the Resource-tell cell as the batch-1 single-device illustration, or delete the tell from this row.

evidence: "they are not operative in their own right, and the LICENSE file at the pinned commit below governs wherever the two differ" and "The operative licence text is not reproduced in this artifact — the paragraphs above are a plain-language summary — so a reader holding only this file must retrieve the grant from the pinned commit."
issue: The distributed artifact is not self-contained with respect to its own license: the file explicitly states the inline bullets are not operative and that the governing license text exists only in an external repository. A reader holding only this file cannot know the actual redistribution terms of the work, and the 'as is' grant is unverifiable offline.
fix_instruction: Reproduce the full LICENSE text verbatim in the artifact (e.g., as a final appendix or on the copyright pages), keeping the pinned-commit URL as a cross-check rather than as the sole carrier of the operative grant.

evidence: "Full terms: https://github.com/zhiqitao/from-token-to-fleet/blob/27f4cd5/LICENSE" and "raw file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhiqitao/from-token-to-fleet/27f4cd5/LICENSE", while the same page states "This edition is built from commit 27f4cd571d53ecb2ac549d5825a77c87f8736ad3 (short 27f4cd5)".
issue: Both license URLs pin a 7-character abbreviated commit, although the edition elsewhere treats the full 40-character hash as the immutable source revision. Short hashes are not collision-proof and do not survive repository rewrites, so the 'immutable' pin that carries the operative license is weaker than the edition's own pinning standard.
fix_instruction: Replace '27f4cd5' with the full commit hash '27f4cd571d53ecb2ac549d5825a77c87f8736ad3' in both URLs, or state explicitly that the short ref is resolvable to the pinned commit and record the resolution date.

chapter: Preface (Evidence cutoff and edition date) vs Ch 1
evidence: Preface: "Primary sources (arXiv reports, model cards, vendor pages) were accessed as of the build date and each is cited with a stable identifier in the References chapter" (build v20260913, dated 2026-09-13) and "Adding a source, or changing a value, is what requires a new build identifier or a named addendum." evidence: Fig 1.1 (p. 33): "[ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] — a schematic of a documented mechanism, not a screenshot or a measurement". Preface contract (p. 21): "[ILLUSTRATIVE] is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical worked example: its inputs are [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and its derived results [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]." Bare tags with no Axis-2 partner: "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]" (Figs 2.1 p. 44, 4.1 p. 112, 5.1 p. 134, 6.1 p. 137), "[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual, roofline developed in Ch 8]" (Fig 2.2 p. 52), "[ILLUSTRATIVE synthetic profile]" (Fig 6.2 p. 140); Figs 3.1/3.2 (pp. 61–62) carry no evidence tag at all.
issue: Caption evidence-tag grammar violates the book's own label contract: [ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] is a pairing the Preface's mapping does not define (ILLUSTRATIVE is restricted to ASSUMPTION/DERIVED results of worked examples, not documented-mechanism schematics); the bare '[ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]' tags lack the mandated one-Axis-1-plus-one-Axis-2 pair; and sibling conceptual figures (3.1, 3.2) are untagged, so identical figure types are treated three different ways.
fix_instruction: Define one figure-schematic convention in the Preface (e.g., permit [ILLUSTRATIVE][FACT] explicitly for documented-mechanism schematics, or introduce a dedicated tag), then apply it uniformly to every conceptual figure including Figs 3.1/3.2, and require the Axis-2 partner on all caption tags.

evidence: §2.8: "decode will be bandwidth-bound (a ~140 GB/token weight-read requiring ~5.6 TB/s sustained over each ~25 ms decode step (aggregate, hypothetical single-device figure; sharded across 8 GPUs it is 17.5 GB/GPU = 700 GB/s per GPU))"; §2.1 (p. 39): "why, at the canonical low-batch operating point, decode is HBM-bandwidth-bound"; vs Table 2-2 (p. 49): "weight-read bandwidth is not the binding constraint at this operating point" (700 GB/s of 3.35 TB/s per GPU, ~21%).
issue: The chapter's summary surfaces restate the decode bottleneck using the hypothetical single-device 5.6 TB/s aggregate that Table 2-2 itself labels 'an aggregate figure, not a per-GPU one' and whose canonical-host verdict is 'bandwidth not binding at this point (weight-read only)'. The take-away an architect carries (size decode for 5.6 TB/s) contradicts the worked example the same chapter just derived.
fix_instruction: Rewrite §2.8 (and qualify §2.1's question) to state the canonical verdict on the per-GPU shard figure (17.5 GB / 3.35 TB/s ≈ 5.2 ms, ~21% of the 25 ms step), reserving 'bandwidth-bound' for the intensity-based regime classification, with the 5.6 TB/s aggregate explicitly marked as the non-deployable single-device illustration.

evidence: "leaving zero true headroom on that two-term model (admission/queueing, tokenization/transfer, network transit, scheduling and first-token sampling sit outside it)" vs the defining convention (p. 40): "It carries no separate 'first decode step' term: under the convention above, the first token's forward pass is sampled inside prefill, so a term for it would count that work twice."
issue: The sentence lists 'first-token sampling' as a term outside the retrieval+prefill budget, directly contradicting the book's defining TTFT convention (stated in the Preface p. 22 and Ch 2 p. 40) under which first-token sampling is inside prefill. It also invents 'network transit' and 'scheduling' as decomposition terms that do not exist in the canonical four-term formula (retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill).
fix_instruction: Delete 'first-token sampling' from the outside-terms list and restrict the enumeration to the canonical remaining terms (admission/queue and tokenization/transfer), or explicitly note any additional unmodeled terms as extensions beyond the defined formula.

evidence: In-figure annotation: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)"; the same page's caption: "the p95 SLO is met (p95 ≈ 0.99 s ≤ 2 s)" and "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget"; Ch 4 (p. 104): "1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to".

fix_instruction: Relabel the annotation to 'p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s' (or 'SLO: p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s') and, if desired, add a separate 1.2 s design-budget marker to the figure.

evidence: "We contrast with a representative MoE model in the Mixtral lineage. Its published model card gives 46.7B total and 12.9B active parameters per token [1P][FACT]." (no model name, URL, revision or access date); "the challenger's attention geometry is [1P][FACT] … the published first-party config of the Mixtral 8x7B-class model" (p. 66); Table 5-2 (p. 123): "9,200 × 0.33 MB; 80 layers × 8 KV heads × head_dim 128 at FP16 (327,680 B/token) [1P][DERIVED]" for "Llama-2/3 70B" and "model card huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 [1P][FACT]" (bare hostname, no scheme); Ch 7 (p. 158): "LLaMA-2 70B, for instance, has 64 query heads but only 8 KV-heads" (uncited). evidence: "The four terms below are the ones a reader meets most often, not the whole vocabulary: Axis 3 also takes SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED and UNMEASURED (all five Axis-3 values are listed in the Axis note below); each term names its axis, and each is the same item as the matching value defined further down this section." Later: "The four terms below are not four values of one axis."
issue: The enumeration invites the exact conflation it later warns against: of the four headlined terms only MEASURED and ANALYTICAL are Axis-3 values, while ILLUSTRATIVE is Axis-1 and HYPOTHESIS is Axis-2, so 'four terms' vs 'five Axis-3 values' can only be reconciled several paragraphs later. The complete Axis-3 vocabulary is buried in a parenthetical rather than presented as the primary list.
fix_instruction: Lead with the five Axis-3 values as a single enumeration, then present the cross-axis highlights (ILLUSTRATIVE, HYPOTHESIS) separately, so the reader never has to infer which of the four terms belong to Axis 3.

evidence: Ch 4: "with the ~140 GB weights and ~64 GB runtime/workspace [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] (the runtime/NCCL/activation reserve derived in Ch 7, which subtracts it to reach the ~436 GB KV budget)". evidence: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]: guardrail latency (PII redaction, refusal checking) on generated 300-token outputs, ~2–8 ms/request on CPU at this chapter's scenario inputs; measure on the target stack (the figure depends on the guardrail implementation and hardware)." vs Note 1 (p. 100): "a hypothesis is tagged [HYPOTHESIS] (Axis 2), never [ILLUSTRATIVE] (Axis 1)" and the Axis-2 definition (p. 20): "ASSUMPTION — a deliberately chosen scenario input".

evidence: Convention (p. 23): "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." Violations: "Ch 4 §4.3 quotes this formula verbatim" (p. 40); "(Ch 3 §3.6, Ch 18)" (p. 74); "matching Ch 4 §4.6" (p. 133); "resident KV slots (Ch 4 §4.3, §4.6)" (p. 136); "(86 in-flight ÷ 17 slots = 5.06 → 6 hosts, Ch 4 §4.3)" (p. 147); "Ch 4 §4.7 tags the same quantity the same way" (p. 153); "(technical note below; Ch 4 §4.3)" (p. 177).
issue: The book's own cross-reference convention prohibits repeating the chapter number after the chapter name, yet the prohibited 'Ch N §N.M' form appears at least seven times across five chapters, while the compliant forms ('Ch 8 §3', '§8.3.3') are also used — the reference apparatus is inconsistent with its own stated rule.
fix_instruction: Normalize every 'Ch N §N.M' occurrence to either '§ N.M' or 'Ch N § M', and add the pattern to the build's lint checklist so future chapters conform.

evidence: "Because a dense model with full multi-head attention gives the cleanest single-constant KV formula (2 × layers × hidden × bytes) and the largest KV footprint — the conservative worst case an architect should always size against first." vs Ch 7 (p. 172): "a model with 100 layers and 12288 dim will have ~4.9 MB/token (2 × 100 × 12288 × 2 B = 4,915,200 B)".
issue: 'The conservative worst case an architect should always size against first' is stated as an absolute, but full-MHA 70B is the worst case only within the canonical 80-layer/8192-hidden geometry; the book itself prints larger per-token KV constants for other geometries (e.g., ~4.9 MB/token). The unscoped superlative could license under-sizing against a bigger-geometry model.
fix_instruction: Scope the claim: 'the largest KV footprint for a given layer count and hidden width — the conservative worst case within the canonical 80-layer/8192-hidden geometry', and cross-reference §7.4's re-derivation examples.

evidence: "24.9 ÷ 8 ≈ 3.1 GB is the per-rank share at 9.5K, read against a single 80 GB rank's HBM" (Fig 7.5 caption, p. 177); "KV offloading — moving some KV state out of GPU HBM (to host DRAM/SSD), trading capacity against transfer latency" (p. 42); declared convention (p. 22): "the worked examples write 'GPU memory' or 'VRAM' for a capacity and 'HBM' for the technology".
issue: Both instances use 'HBM' for a memory capacity (an 80 GB rank's capacity; a pool that KV state is moved out of), contradicting the Preface's declared usage where 'HBM' names the technology and capacities are written 'GPU memory'/'VRAM' — the exact drift the convention says to avoid.
fix_instruction: Rewrite as 'read against a single 80 GB rank's GPU memory' and 'moving some KV state out of GPU memory (HBM) to host DRAM/SSD', and sweep the book for remaining capacity-uses of 'HBM'.

evidence: "Suppose user research and demand modeling independently set the busy-period peak to 50 requests/s (a declared scenario input at this growth scale, not a figure derived from the 500-user count …)" (p. 115) and "With the illustrative ~8.6 s engine response duration, Little's Law implies approximately 50 × 8.6 ≈ 430 requests" (p. 116) — inputs that drive the 26 → 38 → 40 host derivation. fix_instruction: Tag both inputs inline (e.g., '[ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]' for this non-canonical growth variant) at first mention, or state once in the mini-case header that all its inputs carry [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] and its results [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED].

evidence: "actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [2°][HYPOTHESIS] — a rule of thumb, not measured here" vs the Axis-1 definition (p. 20): "[2°] — reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark".

evidence: "Where this panel and that paragraph appear to differ, the stricter reading applies: a number is labeled unless that paragraph's exception test clearly covers it" (p. 19) vs "purely illustrative or rhetorical numbers that no later calculation depends on may carry them in the surrounding prose — the exception test is stated in full in the 'Scope of the labeling' paragraph of the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter" (p. 20).

evidence: "(Mixed-input convention: when a derivation mixes a canonical price with an illustrative rate, the result carries the non-canonical provenance — here the 50 tok/s rate input is [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] while the $20/hr price is canonical (Table 4‑2, a dated price snapshot, [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]).)" vs the front matter's claim (p. 5): "The axes and the full label set are defined in the Preface".
issue: The mixed-input dominance rule — which governs every per-dollar result in Table 5-2 and the §5.3.2 economics — is introduced only as a mid-book parenthetical and appears nowhere in the Preface's evidence-discipline panel that the front matter designates as the definition layer for the label system. A reader applying the Preface alone would not know mixed derivations inherit the non-canonical tag.

evidence: "~85% of 7.08 s on the illustrative 20 ms/token basis — 6.0 s decode of 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode" and, parallel, "~87% of 8.58 s on the canonical 25 ms/token basis — 7.5 s decode of 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode, Ch 4".
issue: Both parentheticals are malformed: '6.0 s decode of 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode' states decode twice and reads as a garbled sum; the intended content is '7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode'. As printed, the sentence asserting the wall-clock split is itself hard to parse, in the chapter's key prefill-vs-decode framing passage.
fix_instruction: Rewrite both parentheticals as 'N% of the T s single-stream window (1.08 s prefill + D s decode)', e.g., '7.08 s = 1.08 s prefill + 6.0 s decode' and '8.58 s = 1.08 s prefill + 7.5 s decode'.
